scope.description: Whole ExifTool breadth across reading, writing, formats and metadata families.
scope.denominator: Reading and writing of EXIF, XMP, IPTC, ICC, MakerNotes, GPS and many hundreds of file formats, composite and print-converted tags, sidecars, geotagging, time shifting, renaming and batch operations, structured and CSV output, configuration and extension.

coverage.rationale: Five-point rubric, whole-application denominator unchanged. Reading is a typed catalogue read by independent EXIF/GPS/IPTC/XMP decoders in JPEG, TIFF, DNG, PNG, WebP and HEIF files and XMP sidecars, with an optional complete native listing, audit and comparison, plus read-only clock reconciliation and typed position and height-reference reports. Writing covers new copies of the same container (JPEG, TIFF, DNG, PNG, WebP and the existing items of HEIF files): descriptive and rights fields, concrete removal categories and a rendering-preserving minimise, the time and location writes (capture-time correction, declared and track-interpolated positions with edition-aware altitude references), and now selected typed metadata carried from a photo or an XMP sidecar onto copies (descriptive, rights, rating, place, camera, lens, exposure with exact numerator and denominator pairs, device serials, a captured time and a position through the E3 writers), each with independent readback, byte-identical image data, a closed native diff and a source-versus-output proof. Beyond the copies, E4 exports portable XMP sidecars in a closed 29-property set (with an explicit altitude reference rule and stated coordinate quantisation), plans photo names from recorded capture facts and makes exact foldered byte copies. Full-block, MakerNote and unknown-tag transfer, editing or merging an existing sidecar, a naming template language, BigTIFF and maker raw containers, video, TIFF and DNG minimise, HEIF item creation and removal, MakerNote editing, extended or structured XMP, reverse geocoding and most of ExifTool remain outside this. The earlier 15 reflected the read family, the JPEG descriptive and removal writes and the time and location families; metadata transfer, sidecar export, naming and organising are further named families in the denominator, which moves the honest rounded value to 20 on the five-point scale, still below the rubric anchor of 25 (a few useful families with major areas missing) and not a claim of whole-application coverage. E5 adds TIFF, DNG, PNG, WebP and HEIF containers to the read family and to every writing operation (editing, removal with PNG and WebP minimise, capture-time and position writes, geotagging, transfer and sidecar application): each is located by a bounded reader, decoded by the shared readers and written as a new copy under an offset-free preservation proof, a shared readback and a closed native diff, with named refusals where native 13.55 or the structure cannot be protected (HEIF items are edited only when they exist and HEIF removal and minimise are refused; TIFF and DNG minimise is a named limit). That moves the honest rounded value to 25, the rubric anchor for a few useful families with major areas missing, and is not a claim of whole-application coverage.

scope.description: Reading, auditing, comparing, editing, removing and minimising the metadata of a bounded set of photographs, and reconciling and correcting capture clocks, locating, setting and geotagging positions, through catalogue-field profiles, transfer groups and policies, a closed naming vocabulary, rule names, a named baseline, typed field edits, removal categories, device groups with declared true times, positions and tracks, with typed CSV handoff to a spreadsheet and produced images handed to later operations.
scope.denominator: User intent and domain decisions within the read/audit/compare workflows over JPEG, TIFF, DNG, PNG, WebP, HEIF and XMP sidecar media sets, the edit, removal and minimise workflows for nine catalogue fields and six removal categories, and the time and location workflows (clock groups, references, corrections, positions, GPX tracks); the E4 copy, sidecar and naming workflows (transfer groups and policies, sidecar export, a closed naming vocabulary and organised copies); editing an existing sidecar, BigTIFF and maker raw containers, authentication and capture-truth judgement are outside this denominator.

abstraction.rationale: Authors state intent as catalogue profiles, field IDs, rule names and a baseline; the adaptor hides Perl invocation, tag and group naming, duplicate/instance keys, JSON number quirks, container location, charset and namespace handling, sidecar pairing, folder expansion with a complete manifest, presence-state classification, literal concordance and anchoring against a fixed native listing. Authors still decide which profiles matter, how to resolve disagreeing sources, whether recorded metadata is believable and what to do with privacy-relevant fields, and the closed catalogue limits what can be asked. For writing, authors state set, clear, add and remove of catalogue fields removal categories and minimise; the adaptor decides destinations, character sets, list joins, language handling, loss policy, native assignments and the three independent proofs, and never accepts a raw tag, option or expression. Confidence stays medium: native evidence is a bounded synthetic corpus. For the time and location workflows authors state devices, true times, shifts and offsets with a keep rule, positions with an explicit height reference and tracks with a gap limit; the adaptor hides time-tag families, sub-second and offset companions, rational coordinate storage, edition-dependent altitude rules, GPX parsing, interpolation and every native assignment, and it never accepts a raw tag, shift expression or geotag option. Authors still decide which clock is right (references are declarations), the group structure, the vertical reference, policies for stale companions and unplaceable photos, and the group and plan names are internal conveniences, so the score is unchanged at 65: more intent is expressed, but some decisions (group naming, assumed offsets, plan hand-off) remain manual. For the E4 workflows authors choose what is carried (closed groups or fields), what to do with existing, absent and ambiguous values, which time basis and source a name uses and what a missing fact means; the adaptor hides the typed snapshot, the catalogue views, native assignments, the sidecar property mapping and anchoring, the sanitiser and collision rules and the create-only copier, and never accepts a native tag, option, template or expression. Authors still decide whether recorded values are believable and which groups are appropriate to share (device serials and location are explicit), and the closed vocabularies limit what can be asked. Confidence stays medium: native evidence is a bounded synthetic corpus. The container family keeps the same intent-level operations, now for every operation: a container choice adds no native option, and its limits surface as stable refusal codes rather than native detail.

limitations: Writes are new copies of the same container (JPEG, TIFF, DNG, PNG, WebP; HEIF only through Exif and XMP items that already exist) for descriptive, rights, removal, time, location, transfer and sidecar application. Items with trailing bytes, extended XMP, MPF, FlashPix, damaged metadata, an XMP value whose qualifiers a rewrite would drop, a paired sidecar or ExifTool warnings are refused per item; an unrecognised maker note blocks device-identity removal (minimise deletes it with the whole Exif block). JPEG, PNG and WebP minimise keeps only Orientation, YCbCrPositioning, ColorSpace and an allow-listed InteropIndex, refuses a capture with a Gamma tag or an XMP rendering value that disagrees with Exif, and lists every kept segment in its residual report; unknown application segments stay byte for byte. Proof N compares listings of the same engine that wrote the file and proves reproducibility, not independent truth; proof P is about bytes and says nothing about pixels or authenticity. Removal is for the listed categories in understood locations and is not anonymisation or privacy certification. No MWG compliance is claimed.

JPEG (any coding process), TIFF, DNG, PNG, WebP, HEIF and XMP sidecars, catalogued fields only; every other tag, container (BigTIFF, maker raw, JPEG XL, GIF) and metadata family is unassessed. Metadata can be wrong and nothing certifies capture time, location, authorship or privacy; sources that disagree are reported, none preferred, and no MWG compliance is claimed. Duplicate source files are refused per item; two distinct files with identical bytes are reported by the audit, not deduplicated. A derived capturedUtc is published as derived even when its local-time input is only partially assessed, and compare treats a zero coordinate with opposite references as the same canonical value.

Native evidence is bounded measurement of a small synthetic corpus: hand-literal qualifier cases, a public agent loop and a Calc folder-handoff/reuse check against ExifTool 13.55 with private fixtures. No kit receipt is registered, no independent acceptance is claimed and the parent gate decides any qualification label. Verification of a native listing needs a configured trusted ExifTool 13.55.

Field coverage is uneven: all 40 catalogue fields have host-literal decoding tests, but modifiedLocal, lensMake and lensSerialNumber are read present from only one synthetic file, and XMP-sourced GPS, structured and extended XMP, MakerNotes, thumbnails and every container outside the six are unassessed. NATIVE_ANCHOR_MISMATCH against a real ExifTool is exercised by one deliberate same-size Make padding (ExifTool trims the trailing space that the independent reader keeps) in a verified partial set, plus retained-listing mutants and stage-emulated host tests; a file that repeats a GPS reference tag is a separate real native case (the field is ambiguous and ExifTool's copies are kept); no other real disagreement is known, and ordinary synthetic fixtures agree.

Discovery matches every query token, so a long natural sentence can find nothing; curated short phrases are reviewed. A folder re-run re-executes every consumer of a re-run producer, even when the published bytes are unchanged.
Subjective source-contract assessment rounded to five points; no exhaustive API denominator supports these percentages.

Time and location: references, assumed offsets, positions, vertical references and track datums are declarations and are not verified; no time zone, daylight-saving rule, leap second, vertical datum conversion or place lookup exists; an interpolated position has no claimed accuracy; the GPS-only 2.4 altitude edition is an inference labelled as such and readers older than Exif 3.0 may not recognise the sea-level references; creating an Exif directory under an untouched height is refused rather than risking a change of its meaning; a sidecar altitude gap, exposure transfer between copies, renaming and reverse geocoding are not provided. Native evidence is a bounded private synthetic corpus run against ExifTool 13.55 (focused host, native, lifecycle, workflow and mutant tests); the global native and union gates and independent acceptance are separate and not claimed here.

Transfer is selected typed values onto copies of JPEG, TIFF, DNG, PNG, WebP and HEIF items: no full-block, MakerNote or unknown-tag transfer, no XMP structures, no merge or edit of an existing sidecar, a destination that records an offset the source lacks or a different fraction precision for a captured time; an Exif block or ExifIFD is never created by a transfer. Names come from recorded capture facts with a closed vocabulary; organised copies exist only inside the run directory, and none of this is privacy or provenance certification.

E5 containers: HEIF metadata items are never created (a conservative, named limit of native 13.55 observed on hand-built fixtures) and HEIF removal and minimise are refused; a HEIF edit that would leave an existing Exif or XMP item empty and an IPTC rebuild of a block with an opaque Photoshop tail (any container, any operation) are refused before native; TIFF and DNG minimise and thumbnails outside JPEG are not offered; a maker note that changed is accepted only when the relocation-aware comparison shows it equal (otherwise MAKERNOTE_CHANGED); items are bounded by 256 MiB (TIFF, DNG) or 64 MiB; BigTIFF, maker raw formats, JPEG XL and GIF are refused. Native evidence is hand-built synthetic fixtures against ExifTool 13.55; the independent family review and the global gates are separate and not claimed here.
